images.title: Equal areas, different shapes
images.purpose: Shows that four parts can have equal area without having the same shape.
images.composition: Before and after: two identical squares side by side with a small gap, same size, same height.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. Each square is 8 by 8 unit cells drawn with a faint grey (#6B7280) grid, 64 cells per square. Columns are numbered 1 to 8 from the left and rows 1 to 8 from the top (numbers not drawn). LEFT square: two thick dark lines through the middle cut it into four 4 by 4 blocks of 16 cells each; top left and bottom right blocks filled teal (#0072B2), top right and bottom left blocks filled amber (#E69F00). RIGHT square: the same four blocks, but each block gives one cell to the next block round in a pinwheel: the top left block also owns cell (row 2, column 5); the top right block also owns cell (row 5, column 7); the bottom right block also owns cell (row 7, column 4); the bottom left block also owns cell (row 4, column 2). So each part loses exactly 1 cell and gains exactly 1 cell, and still has 16 cells. Same colours as the left square for each part (top left and bottom right teal, top right and bottom left amber); the 4 moved cells have a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline. The text 16 is written once in the middle of each of the 8 parts. Under the left square the caption Same shapes; under the right square the caption Different shapes. Above both, centred, the caption Equal areas.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Every part still holds 16 squares, so equal area does not need equal shape.
images.description: Shows that four parts can have equal area without having the same shape.
images.context: Chapter opening hook: infinitely many ways to cut a square into 4 equal areas.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to count the cells in one bumpy part before revealing 16.

image_decisions.why: The hook claim (equal area, unequal shape) is seen at once when the same square is cut two ways with countable cells.
